verification_candidates.claim_text: If you don't fix the thing that caused the leaky gut in the first place, you're never going to get yourself better.
verification_candidates.evidence_quote: You're never going to get yourself better
verification_candidates.rationale: A practical claim that healing leaky gut requires fixing its underlying cause.

verification_candidates.claim_text: 70% of US homes have some kind of mold issue in them.
verification_candidates.evidence_quote: I think the numbers are something like 70% of US homes have some kind of mold issue in them
verification_candidates.rationale: A specific prevalence statistic about mold exposure that listeners might act on.

verification_candidates.claim_text: Mold is a piece or the main driver of 80% of bowel disease.
verification_candidates.evidence_quote: 80% of bowel disease. Mold is a piece or the main driver
verification_candidates.rationale: An empirical claim linking mold to most bowel disease, though ambiguously phrased.

verification_candidates.claim_text: If you fix environmental, toxic and microbial triggers and just eat real food, your gut will patch itself.
verification_candidates.evidence_quote: if you fix those and just eat real food, your gut's going to patch itself
verification_candidates.rationale: A concrete claim that removing triggers plus eating real food can heal the gut.

verification_candidates.claim_text: Eating Activia is doing good for my gut.
verification_candidates.evidence_quote: I'm doing good for my gut
verification_candidates.rationale: A consumer health claim about a probiotic yogurt, quoted and dismissed by the host.

verification_candidates.claim_text: The gut microbiome is a self-regulating ecosystem that balances itself.
verification_candidates.evidence_quote: your gut microbiome is a self-regulating ecosystem. That means it balances itself
verification_candidates.rationale: A causal model of microbiome regulation offered as the basis for the advice.

verification_candidates.claim_text: Candida overgrowth is normal microbes overgrowing because they are opportunistic.
verification_candidates.evidence_quote: the candida overgrowth, these are all normal microbes in our body, but they are overgrowing because they are what's called opportunistic
verification_candidates.rationale: A mechanism claim about candida overgrowth that shapes treatment advice.

verification_candidates.claim_text: The gut's self-regulating system becomes dysregulated because you have too much of something or not enough of something, such as environmental toxins, stress, or food.
verification_candidates.evidence_quote: the self-regulating system becomes dysregulated because you have too much of something or not enough of something
verification_candidates.rationale: A broad causal claim about what creates gut dysbiosis.

verification_candidates.claim_text: Even a single dose of antibiotics can prevent certain bacteria from ever coming back.
verification_candidates.evidence_quote: even a single dose of antibiotics can prevent certain bacteria from ever coming back
verification_candidates.rationale: A specific, checkable claim about antibiotics permanently altering the microbiome.

verification_candidates.claim_text: Antibiotics might eliminate certain bacteria entirely.
verification_candidates.rationale: A stronger version of the antibiotic-microbiome claim, hedged as possibility.

verification_candidates.claim_text: Probiotics are not really what they're cracked up to be.
verification_candidates.evidence_quote: I don't think probiotics are really what they're cracked up to be
verification_candidates.rationale: A dismissive efficacy claim about probiotic supplements.

verification_candidates.claim_text: Your food and your environment determine your gut microbiome, so fixing them lets the gut fix itself.
verification_candidates.evidence_quote: your food and your environments determine that gut microbiome anyways. So if you can fix those, it'll fix itself
verification_candidates.rationale: A causal claim that diet and environment, not probiotics, determine the microbiome.
